findings.what: Retire without the write skip undoes itself: the write of the ended turn's own reply re-queues the whole chain that was just retired, and the acks mark it stored again.
findings.scenario:
Switches: TRACK_STORED and RETIRE_ENDED_PAGES on, SKIP_ENDED_WRITES off (resolve_retention_switches grants this). At the commit of an explicit end, retire_storage_chain zeroes every stored own node and clears its stored mark. The reply inserted a moment earlier still has its host copy in flight, so it is left to its ack (_retire_at_ack). On the next pass that copy's ack calls write_backup_storage(reply), and the heal takes unstored_ancestors(reply): every retired node is host-backed, unstored and has no write queued, so the whole chain is queued again ahead of the reply. With skip-stored writes the write thread stamps those files to now; without it, it rewrites them. Their acks mark them stored again; only the reply ends at mtime zero.

Run on the real CPU tree (review_threads/zz_review_threads_retire_heal.py): the writes queued after the retire are [reply_1, prompt_2, tail] where [tail] is expected, and reply_1 and prompt_2 are stored again after the acks. With SKIP_ENDED_WRITES on and both inserts of the last turn flagged, nothing is re-queued and both sets end empty (same file), so the planned four-switch arm with reply keys from the hint is not hit.

Size at campaign 34's ec_full: 483,910 files (15.5 M tokens) of own pages re-queued against 32.1 M tokens inserted. Each end adds the session's own chain (p50 21.7 K, p90 59 K tokens) to pending_backup_tokens, next to a 50 K read hold.

By reading only: with reply keys read from the reply, the last prompt is not skipped, and a prompt copy still in flight at the commit takes the same path. The engineer's test_retire_takes_the_replies_no_later_prompt_repeated stops before the tail's ack, so it does not see this.
findings.fix: In write_backup_storage, skip the heal when node_id is in _retire_at_ack: an ended session's page needs no chain above it. (Or do not write such a node at all, which is R1 for the tail; that changes what a retire-only arm writes, so it is the author's call.) Add the case above as a test in TestStoredMarksOnACpuTree. Until then, make resolve_retention_switches refuse RETIRE_ENDED_PAGES without SKIP_ENDED_WRITES.

findings.what: The report's bound "a page is touched at most once per interval" does not hold: a node read back from the SSD starts stale (-inf), and one stale node re-stamps every stored node of the chain.
findings.scenario:
Each landed storage read adds nodes through insert_host with storage_touched_at = -inf (line 158; marked stored at line 2266). At the turn's next request match, any(...) at line 2691 is true, and every stored node on the path is returned and re-stamped, however recently its ancestors were touched.

Run on the CPU tree (review_threads/zz_review_threads_refresh.py): with a 300 s interval, three turns 10 s apart that each read one more node back touch 3, 4 and 5 pages; the head's two pages are touched all three times.

Campaign 34's ec_full had 6,157 gate reads and 1,858 re-reads (out/reread_volume_c34.out). At its mean chain of 391 pages and two files a page, that is about 6.3 M utime calls (my estimate), against the 1.72 M the report takes from the plan.

The cost is small where I could measure it: 2.2 us of path building and 2.8 us of utime per file in a temp dir, so about 30 s of touch-thread time in the run; the scheduler-side walk takes 5 us on a 60-node chain (about 3 % of a match). The journal load on the SSD volume is not measured.
findings.fix: Correct the claim in the report and in the docstring of test_a_stale_tail_takes_its_fresh_head_along_and_a_second_match_takes_nothing, and expect l3_touch files= at several times 239/s in the first arm. If the bound is wanted: keep each node's last stamp in wall-clock ns and give a stale tail stamps just below its nearest fresh ancestor's, instead of re-stamping the fresh ancestors. Add a test with a read-back tail under a fresh head.

findings.what: No test or mutation guards the try/except that keeps the touch thread alive after a failing job.
findings.scenario:
No test makes stamp_pages or _page_file_paths raise, and mutations.py has no entry for the touch loop's except. So moving the stamp call out of the try at lines 938-946 leaves every test green. After that change, the first unexpected exception ends the thread; touch_pages keeps queuing into a SimpleQueue that nobody drains; refresh and retire stop with no log line, and l3_touch simply disappears.

The current code is right. I ran the missing case on a real HiCacheNixl in a temp dir (review_threads/zz_review_threads_touch_thread.py): a first job that raises is logged as "NIXL L3 touch failed", the next job zeroes its page, and close() stops the thread.
findings.fix: Add that case to TestNixlTouch in test_hicache_nixl_storage.py (first job raises, second job is applied, the warning is logged, no touch thread after close) and a mutation for it.

findings.what: With PP > 1 the stored verdict is not the minimum over ranks: a later PP rank's own short write is overwritten by PP rank 0's verdict.
findings.scenario:
_agree_stored calls _all_reduce, which reduces over TP on PP rank 0 only and then runs _pp_sync; on PP rank > 0, torch.distributed.recv writes rank 0's tensor over the local votes.

Run with a patched recv (review_threads/zz_review_threads_pp.py): on PP rank 1 a write acked one token short gives the local vote [0], and the node is finished as stored: (1, 0, True).

The ranks agree, so the trees do not diverge. But the node counts as stored although rank 1's layers are short, and the heal never rewrites it. The docstring says "on every rank", the report says "agreed over ranks", and the plan asks for the minimum over ranks. TP > 1 at PP = 1 is a true minimum.
findings.fix: Either refuse TRACK_STORED when pp_size > 1 in resolve_retention_switches, or reduce the votes over the PP group as well (the PP sync runs one way, so it needs its own collective). At the least, correct the docstring and the name of test_a_write_short_on_any_rank_is_unstored_on_every_rank.

findings.what: The FULL-only dependency of retire is resolved before a draft model's sidecar pools are registered, so retire can be granted on a cache whose pages have files the touch never reaches.
findings.scenario:
kv_cache_builder.py lines 404-412 run create_tree_cache (init_hicache, then _init_storage_retention) and only afterwards maybe_register_hicache_draft, which appends to sidecar_pool_specs through register_sidecar_pool. With a draft model that is not packed (HiCacheDraftMode.SIDECAR; a standalone draft is not EAGLE, so the prefetcher accepts it), full_kv_only is True at start-up: the start-up line reads retire_ended_pages=1 with no warning. Each page then has a draft sidecar file that _page_file_paths does not name, and the cleaner ranks a page by its newest file, so a retired page keeps its old place. The same server resolves retire off after a runtime re-attach.

By reading only; not run (those paths need a GPU). The order of the two calls is also visible in test_decode_retraction_backup.py lines 173-180.
findings.fix: Call _init_storage_retention() at the end of register_sidecar_pool once init_hicache has run (the prefetcher is created later, so it picks up the result), and add a test with a sidecar registered after init.

findings.what: The default-off claim "same outcome in all 122 files" carries no signal for the real init_hicache and attach paths: the tests that reach them cannot run on CPU.
findings.scenario:
With every switch off, _init_storage_retention() still runs in init_hicache and after each attach, and HiCacheNixl.__init__ still runs the two new getters. The only tests that call the real init_hicache are test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py (1,234 failed, 46 passed, 1,511 skipped; I reran it and got the same counts) and test_decode_retraction_backup.py (10 failed, 4 passed). Their failures are "No accelerator" and "No CUDA GPUs are available", before and after the change.

By reading, the off path is sound: cache_controller.storage_backend exists from HiCacheController.__init__, get_memory() is already used at the top of init_hicache, and nothing is logged unless a switch is asked for. No test confirms it on a real cache.
findings.fix: Run these two files on the GPU when the running campaign frees it, before the first arm; or start the off arm first and compare its start-up lines and HICACHE_EVT line formats with campaign 34's.

findings.what: With a touch switch on, the thread keeps its backend alive, and close() hides a thread that did not stop.
findings.scenario:
The thread's target is a bound method. Run in review_threads/zz_review_threads_touch_thread.py: a backend dropped without close() survives del and gc.collect() with its thread (alive, 1 touch thread), where with the switches off it is collected and __del__ closes it (not alive, 0 threads). The controller's attach-failure, detach and atexit paths all call close(), so this needs a caller that forgets it, such as a test.

close() at lines 648-652 puts the stop marker behind the queued jobs and joins for 5 s. On a timeout (a long backlog, or a utime hung on a network file system: the same code serves 3FS and GDS) it drops the handle with no log line; the thread then goes on with the jobs queued before the stop, including after a re-attach.

A process that exits without close(), with 2,000 jobs queued, exits cleanly: return code 0, no hang, nothing created (zz_review_threads_exit.py).
findings.fix: Pass the queue to the thread as an argument, log a warning when the thread is still alive after the join, and consider a stop flag so that close() discards queued jobs.

verdict:
**Switches off: safe to run, by reading.** The off path of the real init and attach has no GPU test behind it yet.
- The patch replaces 14 lines of HEAD and adds the rest; I read every one. Off, the added code that still runs is inert: two env reads and two attributes in HiCacheNixl.__init__ (no thread, no log), one _init_storage_retention() at init_hicache and at attach (no log), one comparison per match_prefix, a False flag per insert, three node fields that nothing reads, and two False flags in the prefetcher that keep _end_session's old body.
- The only changed log line is h2s_done, which now appends an empty string when off; it is byte-identical and a test pins it. No hook is bound and no file is touched.
- All ten named files give the reported counts, including the 7-minute file (1,234 failed for want of a GPU, 46 passed, 1,511 skipped). Nine more files of the folder match the engineer's table.
- Four HEAD tests from outside the folder (scheduler attach and events, invariant checker, decode tree core) pass on the copy's engine; the engineer ran only the mem_cache folder.

**Switches on, the planned four-switch arm (TP = 1, FULL-only, write-through, reply keys from the hint): safe to run for two hours as far as threads and ordering go.**
- The tree is touched only on the scheduler thread; the touch thread gets copied key lists and builds paths itself; no file system call was added to the scheduler thread.
- Checked on a real HiCacheNixl in temp dirs: a failing job is logged and the next one runs; close() runs the queued jobs and joins; a touch after close is dropped; missing files create nothing and are counted gone; an idle thread blocks without spinning; a process exits cleanly without close().
- A busy touch thread leaves the main thread 98 % of its Python time.
- Retire at the ack keeps a zeroing behind its own write; the one path that breaks this order is the bug below.
- Expect l3_touch files= at several times the report's 239/s, because every turn that reads history back re-touches its whole chain.

**Do not run RETIRE_ENDED_PAGES without SKIP_ENDED_WRITES until the first finding is fixed.** That combination undoes its own retire and re-queues about 15.5 M tokens of writes at ec_full's volume. Reply keys read from the reply expose a rarer form of the same path.

**Not covered by anything:** TP > 1, PP > 1 (the stored verdict ignores later PP ranks), a draft model with sidecar pools, and the merge with copy A.

**Base moved.** The real tree gained the prefill load hold at 3:37-3:43 PM ET and, at 5:51 PM ET, a keep_touched option in nixl_cleaner.py with its test. The task's diff commands show those as reverse hunks; they are not this change. Copy B is HEAD b7074d9cae plus steps_1_3.patch byte for byte, with nixl_cleaner.py, scheduler.py, tokenizer_manager.py and model_runner.py equal to HEAD, and it did not change during the review.
